title: WebSocketMultiplayerPeer CreateClient returns Ok despite failing
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: 4.5.beta1

### System information

Godot v4.5.beta1.mono - Fedora Linux 42 (KDE Plasma Desktop Edition) on Wayland - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3080 Ti (nvidia; 575.57.08) - AMD Ryzen 7 5800X 8-Core Processor (16 threads) - 31.25 GiB memory

### Issue description

When using the `WebSocketMultiplayerPeer` and calling `CreateClient` with invalid host information, the return value is `Error.Ok` despite the connection not being properly created.

If using `ENetMultiplayerPeer` instead, failing to connect will result in an error value.

I expected to get an error result with the web socket as well instead of failing silently.
I looked at the documentation and didn't see any hint about this happening.

### Steps to reproduce

- Create host with `WebSocketMultiplayerPeer`
- Attempt to create client with `WebSocketMultiplayerPeer` connecting to the host, but use incorrect address value
- `Ok` is returned despite failing

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

Simply export the project, start twice (in the terminal), press host button in one window and client button in the other.
I added ENet versions which do report a connection error and web socket versions which incorrectly report success. 
Obviously, mixing the two versions is not meaningful.

[websocket_peer_issue_mrp.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/20835518/websocket_peer_issue_mrp.zip)

Since a GDScript version is preferred, I asked GPT to translate my C# code and it looks somewhat reasonable and seems to show the same issue, but I cannot guarantee that the GDScript version is fully equivalent. 
Both scripts are contained.
